findings.claim: The caption file now always crosses a filesystem in production, through shutil.move's copy2 fallback, and no test exercises that path.
findings.impact: Refreshing captions on a drive where copying fails part-way (disk full) truncates the existing <title>.vtt in place, where the old same-directory rename could not. On a mount that refuses chmod or utime on the destination, the content is copied but copystat raises, so the caller records captions_downloaded false while a good .vtt is on disk.
findings.evidence: addons/media_import/backend/service.py:243 creates the scratch directory in the system temp location and service.py:264 moves from it to the drive. decisions.md records /tmp/mi_captions_*/captions.en.vtt inside the container, separate from the bind-mounted drive. The exception reaches service.py:968, which leaves captions_ok False. The tests in test_nfc_names.py use pytest tmp_path, normally on the same filesystem as tempfile's directory, so os.rename succeeds there and the copy branch does not run. _dedup_rolling_vtt (service.py:266) also rewrites the file afterwards, and I did not read how it writes, so the old code may have had a similar exposure at that later step.
findings.repro: not_reproduced; found by reading. Suggested check: patch os.rename to raise OSError(EXDEV) and make shutil.copystat raise PermissionError, then observe the (False/exception) outcome with a complete vtt_path on disk.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared and the happy path was verified in the app. The failure needs a full disk or a restrictive mount, so this is an edge condition rather than normal use.

findings.proposed_fix: Copy the file content to a temporary name in the destination directory with shutil.copyfile, then os.replace it onto vtt_path, so the old captions stay intact until the new file is complete and no chmod or utime is needed.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change, so there is no declared touch-point list and the first-review question cannot be answered against one. I raised no 'unplanned place' findings because nothing defines what was planned.

Places the diff reaches, for the record: addons/media_import pointer bump; backend/service.py::_download_captions_sync; frontend/Composer.tsx; tests test_listing_call_inventory.py, test_loft_caption_state.py, test_nfc_names.py and Composer.test.tsx; docs/developer-guide/known-issues.md.

Places reached indirectly without a diff: subscription/providers/youtube.py::fetch_transcript through _download_captions_sync_for_provider. It reads <stem>.vtt from its own temporary directory after the call (youtube.py:579-587), which the new code still produces. The link-import caller at service.py:965 also keeps its contract, and its parent directory exists because it is derived from the .loft path.

The listing inventory entry is correct. The new glob at service.py:261 lists a private scratch directory with a fixed pattern and uses no stored name, so LISTING_ONLY is the right class, and the scanner key (service.py, _download_captions_sync, glob) with count 1 matches the code.

docs/specs/nfc-tolerant-name-matching.md still describes the old mechanism (I6, I12 and the `.*.vtt` touch-point line). This is a historical spec, and the code is authoritative, so it is not reported as a defect.
potential_unspecified_behavior: If /subscriptions/resolve fails, the Composer sends a channel URL to createLoft, both after a failed preview (cached as unknown at Composer.tsx:153) and at submit (Composer.tsx:181). The tests encode this behavior. The resolve route does pure parsing (router.py:291-301), so in normal use the failure mostly coincides with /link failing too, and I did not raise it as a finding.

A preview that answers after a successful submit still runs setKind and writes classified.current (Composer.tsx:143-144), so the empty composer can show Subscribe and the display-mode field until the next URL. The same stale setKind existed before this change. It affects display only, because submit now decides from its own classification.
classified.current is keyed by URL only, not by drive. The resolve route's classification does not depend on the drive, so a drive change without remount does not produce a wrong kind today.

A folder filled in by an earlier URL's preview stays selected for the next URL, and rememberFolder then writes it under the new kind (Composer.tsx:174, 205). decisions.md observed this. The folder-retaining condition is unchanged from the old code and the folder is visible in the picker.
regression_risks: The Composer submit path now awaits a network call before dispatching. That call has no timeout in the code I read (api.ts:219 onward), so a hung resolve would leave the composer in the submitting state. Resolve is local parsing, so this needs a stuck backend.
The URL input is not disabled during submit, so text typed during the wait is cleared by setUrl("") on success (Composer.tsx:208). This predates the change, but the wait is now slightly longer.
Captions are written to the system temp location first, which adds a dependency on temp-space availability that the old in-folder write did not have.
test_coverage: Backend: the neighbour case in test_nfc_names.py would fail if the `<title>.*.vtt` lookup returned, because <stem>.3.0.2.ja.vtt would be selected and renamed. Changing outtmpl back to the drive would also fail, because the scratch glob would find nothing.

Backend gaps: no test asserts that the scratch directory is removed, none covers an exception raised by the move or by _dedup_rolling_vtt, and the cross-filesystem copy branch does not run (see CR-1).

The `metacharacters-and-nfd` parameter in test_nfc_names.py no longer contains any NFD input, since the NFD lang file was removed. No listing depends on it now, so this is a naming residue rather than a behavior gap.

Frontend: dropping the `done.url === trimmed` comparison fails the 'finished for a previous URL' case, removing the submit-time resolve fails 'debounce pending', and removing the remembered-folder line fails 'uses the remembered folder'.

Frontend gaps: removing `classified.current = null` would likely survive; it looks behaviorally equivalent because a re-pasted URL gets the same classification. No test covers the late-preview display state after submit, or asserts rememberFolder's arguments in the submit-time classification path; I did not read the existing write-back tests to confirm the latter.
not_verified: I ran no tests or mutations; this review has read-only tools, so the kill and survive statements come from reading the code.
I did not observe the behavior of shutil.move on a real cross-filesystem mount or on restrictive NAS mounts.
I did not read yt-dlp's source to confirm the subtitle filename; I relied on the path sampled in decisions.md (captions.en.vtt).
I did not read how _dedup_rolling_vtt writes its output, beyond its first lines.
I did not read Composer.test.tsx outside the diff, including its top-level mock reset and existing folder write-back tests, or the app-run artifacts cited by decisions.md.
I did not check whether a spec for this change is required or exists in docs/specs/INDEX.md.
